meaning:
1) to supplant, circumvent, take by the heel, follow at the heel, assail insidiously, overreach
1a) (Qal) to supplant, overreach, attack at the heel
1b) (Piel) to hold back

elsewhere.note: He said, “Isn’t he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my blessing.” He said…
After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.
“Everyone beware of his neighbor, and don’t trust in any brother; for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbor will go around like a slanderer.
In the womb he took his brother by the heel; and in his manhood he contended with God.
